The provided data offers a comprehensive national overview of clinical quality indicator results for acute surgery in [[danmark|Danmark]], tracking performance across three distinct periods: the current period (01.09.2024–31.08.2025), 2023/24, and 2022/23 [^src1]. The evaluation covers ten specific indicators, measuring everything from timely antibiotic administration and imaging to postoperative mobilization and mortality rates [^src1].

**Leaders and Trailers**
Among the shared measures, [[indikator-4y|Indikator 4y]] (surgery within 24 hours for patients without perforation, ischemia, or bleeding) is the clear leader, achieving an 81.7% fulfillment rate in the current period [^src1]. [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] (epidural placement during surgery) also posts a relatively strong national average of 51.7% [^src1]. Conversely, [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] (preoperative optimization or direct to surgery) trails significantly, reaching only 14.3% in the current period [^src1]. [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] (postoperative monitoring for elderly or severely ill patients) also struggles, sitting at a national average of 22.3% [^src1].

**Targets Met and Missed**
The vast majority of indicators miss their stated national targets. For example, [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] (antibiotics within 3 hours) has a target of >60% but only achieved 35.6%, and [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]] (CT scan within 120 minutes) targets ≥90% but reached just 33.5% [^src1]. However, the mortality indicators present a different picture. [[indikator-9|Indikator 9]] (30-day mortality) has an upper-limit target of <12%, and the current national rate is 10.1%, successfully falling below the threshold [^src1]. Similarly, [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]] (90-day mortality) targets <18% and achieved 13.7%, also meeting the national standard [^src1]. Despite these national averages meeting the mortality thresholds, the "%" column—which reflects the proportion of individual departments meeting the targets—remains at 0 for both [^src1].

**Trends Across Periods**
Several indicators show notable trends over the three recorded periods. [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] (mobilization within 24 hours) demonstrates strong, consistent improvement, rising from 27.9% in 2022/23 to 34.4% in 2023/24, and reaching 41.5% in the current period [^src1]. [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] also shows steady growth, doubling from 7.0% to 14.3% over the same timeframe [^src1]. Mortality rates have also improved (decreased): 30-day mortality ([[indikator-9|Indikator 9]]) dropped from 11.7% to 10.1%, and 90-day mortality ([[indikator-10|Indikator 10]]) fell from 16.5% to 13.7% [^src1]. On the other hand, [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] (epidural placement) experienced a slight decline from 52.6% to 51.7%, and [[indikator-4y|Indikator 4y]] dipped marginally from its 2023/24 peak of 82.4% to 81.7% [^src1].

**Outliers**
An interesting outlier is found in [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]]. While its national average (22.3%) falls far short of the ≥80% target, it is the only indicator in the dataset where the "%" column registers a value other than 0, showing a 4 [^src1]. This suggests that while the national aggregate is low, a small fraction (4%) of departments might be successfully meeting the stringent monitoring requirements for this specific cohort.
